documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

CC: Here to establish care. Leaving her previous primary care office after it changed hands; records release signed today.

HPI: 54-year-old woman, office administrator, with several long-running issues, all fairly settled.
- Hypertension: on metoprolol succinate 50, amlodipine 10 and HCTZ 25 for years. Checks at the pharmacy kiosk now and then, usually 130s/80s. No headaches, chest pain or swelling.
- Type 2 diabetes: told years ago; managed with diet only, never on medication. Tries to keep carbs down at lunch. No polyuria, no foot numbness.
- Cholesterol: atorvastatin 40, aspirin 81. No muscle aches.
- Bipolar I disorder and depression: followed by her outside psychiatrist, who prescribes lithium 300 twice daily and sertraline 100. Mood steady for a long while. Psychiatry has been getting lithium levels; she would like us to do her blood work here and copy them.

PMH: as above. No surgeries.
Meds: metoprolol succinate 50 daily, amlodipine 10 daily, HCTZ 25 qAM, atorvastatin 40 daily, ASA 81 daily, lithium carbonate 300 BID, sertraline 100 daily.
Allergies: shellfish (cannot remember what happened, avoids it).
FH: father with hypertension and type 2 diabetes. Mother with high cholesterol, had a stroke at 68. Maternal aunt with bipolar disorder. Brother had an MI at 52.
SH: lives alone in Florence. Never smoked. A drink or two a month, socially. Works full time in an office.

ROS: negative except as in HPI.

Exam: vitals in flowsheet. Well appearing, pleasant. HEENT unremarkable, no thyromegaly. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Extremities without edema; feet with intact skin, good pulses, monofilament intact bilaterally. Neuro grossly nonfocal, no tremor.

A/P:
1. Hypertension, at goal today on three drugs. Continue.
2. Type 2 diabetes, diet-controlled. A1c and urine albumin today. Will want yearly eye exam; she has an optometrist.
3. Hyperlipidemia. Continue atorvastatin 40 and aspirin. Lipids today.
4. Bipolar I disorder / depression, stable with psychiatry. Lithium level, TSH, calcium and creatinine today; results will be faxed to psychiatry.
5. Health maintenance: hep C and HIV screens offered and accepted. Prior records requested for colonoscopy, Pap and vaccines. Mammogram ordered. Flu shot when supply arrives next month.

RTC 6 months, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Ms. Desrosiers, your labs from Tuesday look good. A1c is in the diabetes range but stable with diet alone, so no medication needed. Cholesterol is well controlled on the atorvastatin. Kidney function, calcium and thyroid are normal, and your lithium level is right in the usual range; I've faxed a copy to your psychiatrist. Hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative. Talk soon.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Overdue follow-up (last seen 9/2022). Two things today.
1) She read about a cardiovascular prevention study recruiting locally, testing a new cholesterol drug against standard statin treatment, and wants to know if she should sign up. Her brother's heart attack at 52 is very much on her mind.
2) BP readings at home creeping up this winter, mostly 140s/90ish. Taking all three BP meds every morning. No headache, CP, SOB.
Mood stable. No tremor.

O: BP elevated today, recheck similar. Heart RRR, lungs clear, no edema.

A/P:
1. Hypertension above goal on metoprolol succinate 50, amlodipine 10, HCTZ 25. With diabetes, adding lisinopril 10 mg daily. Reviewed common side effects including cough and, rarely, lip or tongue swelling (stop and call). BMP in 2 weeks for potassium and creatinine.
2. Research question: talked through what joining a randomized trial would mean, including that she could be assigned to the study drug in place of her atorvastatin or kept on standard treatment, that neither she nor I would choose, and that she can withdraw at any time. Gave her the study contact information to call herself. Fine to stay on atorvastatin 40 and aspirin either way.
3. T2DM, diet: A1c today.
4. Lithium level today (due), copy to psychiatry.

RTC 3 months, BP log in the meantime.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Potassium and kidney function are normal two weeks into the lisinopril. Keep taking it and keep the BP log going.

documents.title: Office Visit: Cough
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: cough x 2 months.

HPI: Dry, tickly cough that started roughly 4 weeks after she began lisinopril in February and has not let up since, about two months now. Worse lying down and when talking on the phone at work. Nothing coming up. No fever, no shortness of breath, no wheezing, no chest pain. No heartburn. No new exposures at home or work. No lip, tongue or throat swelling at any point. Never smoked.

Meds: lisinopril 10 (since 2/15), metoprolol succinate 50, amlodipine 10, HCTZ 25, atorvastatin 40, ASA 81, lithium 300 BID, sertraline 100.

Exam: BP 132/84, HR 78, RR 16, afebrile, sat normal. No distress, speaking full sentences with an occasional dry cough. Oropharynx clear. Lungs with good air movement, no wheezes, rales or rhonchi. Heart regular. No edema. Remainder unremarkable.

A/P:
1. Cough, almost certainly from the ACE inhibitor given the timing and a normal exam. Stop lisinopril today; it can take a few weeks to settle. ACE inhibitors added to her intolerance list. CXR to be thorough given two months of symptoms; CBC and BMP today.
2. Hypertension: well controlled with lisinopril on board, so expect readings to rise off it. Continue the other three. Home log, BP visit in about 2 months.
Call if cough is not clearly better in 3-4 weeks.

reports.text: PA and lateral chest. No prior for comparison. Lungs are clear without consolidation, mass or effusion. No pneumothorax. Heart size normal. Mediastinal contours and hila unremarkable. Osseous structures intact.

documents.title: Test Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your chest x-ray is clear, and your blood counts, electrolytes and kidney function are normal (creatinine 1.0). That fits with the lisinopril being the cause of the cough. Stay off it and let me know how you are doing in a few weeks.

documents.title: Nephrology Consultation
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Outside nephrology consultation, date of service 10/11/2023.

Reason for referral: resistant hypertension.

Thank you for referring Ms. Desrosiers, a 56-year-old woman with hypertension, diet-treated type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia and bipolar I disorder on lithium. Her pressures were well controlled earlier this year with lisinopril added, which was stopped in May because of cough. Over roughly the five months since, her readings have stayed high despite reliable use of metoprolol succinate, amlodipine and hydrochlorothiazide. She has no chest pain, palpitations or headaches.

Medications: metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, amlodipine 10 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily, lithium carbonate 300 mg BID, sertraline 100 mg daily.
Allergies: ACE inhibitors (cough); shellfish.
Family history: father with hypertension and diabetes; brother with MI at 52.

Exam: BP 162/98 seated. Comfortable. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen: a prominent bruit is heard just to the right of the umbilicus. No edema.

Data: creatinine 1.2 mg/dL (up from 1.0 in May), BUN 22, potassium 3.4 (low). Abdominal ultrasound with Doppler today: right kidney smaller than the left.

Assessment: resistant hypertension with an abdominal bruit, an asymmetric small right kidney, low potassium on a thiazide and a creatinine rise. This is right renal artery stenosis until proven otherwise.

Plan:
1. Renal vein renin sampling with interventional radiology, and serum aldosterone.
2. Continue current antihypertensives. Increase dietary potassium (bananas, potatoes, beans); recheck BMP in about 2 months with her PCP.
3. Will see her again with results.

Outside nephrology

documents.title: Renal Vein Renin Sampling
documents.author: interventional radiology
documents.body:
Outside interventional radiology procedure report, 11/08/2023.

Procedure: selective bilateral renal vein and infrarenal IVC sampling for renin.
Access: right common femoral vein under ultrasound guidance, moderate sedation.
Samples drawn from right renal vein, left renal vein and infrarenal IVC; serum aldosterone sent from IVC sample.
Results: renin activity high in the right renal vein sample and low (suppressed) on the left. Serum aldosterone elevated.
Complications: none. Hemostasis with manual compression. Discharged home after 2 hours of bed rest.
Impression: lateralization of renin secretion to the right kidney.

documents.title: Nephrology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Outside nephrology follow-up, 11/21/2023, telephone.

Reviewed renal vein renin sampling with Ms. Desrosiers: renin is high from the right kidney and suppressed on the left, with elevated aldosterone. Together with the small right kidney and the bruit, this supports right renal artery stenosis as the driver of her hypertension.

We discussed management. For now, medical therapy: continue metoprolol succinate 50, amlodipine 10, hydrochlorothiazide 25, plus atorvastatin and aspirin. Low-salt, potassium-rich diet. Please check a BMP in December. Return to nephrology as needed or sooner if her kidney function changes.

Outside nephrology

documents.title: Cardiology Research Clinic Letter
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology, research clinic visit 04/12/2024.

Dear colleague,

I met Ms. Desrosiers, 57, at your referral to discuss our randomized study of an investigational lipid-lowering agent compared with standard statin therapy. She is motivated by her brother's myocardial infarction at 52. She has hypertension with right renal artery stenosis followed by nephrology, diet-controlled type 2 diabetes and hyperlipidemia on atorvastatin 40 mg, and takes aspirin 81 mg.

She denies exertional chest discomfort, dyspnea, palpitations or syncope.

Exam: well appearing. Heart regular, normal S1 and S2, no murmur or gallop. Lungs clear. No carotid bruits. No edema. Peripheral pulses intact.

We reviewed the protocol, the randomization, the visit schedule and the possibility of coming off atorvastatin if assigned to the study drug. After taking the consent documents home, she called on 04/16 to say she has decided not to enroll. That is entirely reasonable.

Recommendations: continue atorvastatin 40 mg and aspirin 81 mg. Continued blood pressure management with you and nephrology. No cardiology follow-up needed unless symptoms arise.

Outside cardiology

documents.title: Emergency Department Physician Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Outside emergency department record, date of service 04/24/2025.

CC: vomiting, diarrhea, shaky hands, confusion.

HPI: 58-year-old woman with bipolar I disorder on lithium, hypertension and right renal artery stenosis. For two days she has had nausea with repeated vomiting, loose stools and a tremor in both hands. Since yesterday she has felt foggy and mixed up, and walking has been hard because she feels off balance. She mentions she started a new medicine recently but cannot think of its name and did not bring her bottles.

Meds (per patient and pharmacy list): lithium carbonate 300 mg BID, sertraline 100 mg daily, metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, amlodipine 10 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily.
Allergies: ACE inhibitors, shellfish.

Exam: vitals within normal limits (BP 128/76, HR 84, RR 16, T 36.9 C, SpO2 98% RA). Awake, slow to answer, oriented to person and place. Fine bilateral hand tremor at rest and with posture. Mildly ataxic on finger-nose and gait. No clonus. Mucous membranes dry. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender.

Results: lithium 2.5 mmol/L (reference 0.6-1.2). Creatinine 1.1. Sodium 140, potassium 4.2, calcium 9.6.

MDM: lithium toxicity, symptomatic with neurological findings. Lithium held. Normal saline started, ondansetron for nausea. No indication for dialysis at present with good urine output. Placed in observation for serial levels and neuro checks.

Outside hospital admission 09/17/2025 to 09/19/2025.

Principal diagnosis: acute (flash) pulmonary edema.

Presentation: 58-year-old woman with hypertension, right renal artery stenosis on medical therapy, diet-controlled type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia and bipolar I disorder on lithium. Woke at about 2 am acutely short of breath and could not lie flat. EMS found her hypertensive and hypoxic. On arrival BP 176/100, SpO2 89% on room air. Chest x-ray showed pulmonary edema. Troponin normal (6 ng/L). NT-proBNP 1,240 pg/mL. Creatinine 1.3.

Course: treated with supplemental oxygen and IV furosemide with rapid improvement; on room air by the afternoon of admission. Transthoracic echocardiogram: normal LV size and systolic function, EF 60%, no significant valve disease. Lithium level not checked; she had no tremor or confusion.

Discharge medications: unchanged home regimen: metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, amlodipine 10 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily, lithium carbonate 300 mg BID, sertraline 100 mg daily.
Allergies: ACE inhibitors (cough), shellfish.

Follow-up: PCP in one week; outpatient nephrology regarding her renal artery stenosis.

documents.author: interventional radiology
documents.body:
Outside interventional radiology procedure note, 10/13/2025.

Indication: recurrent flash pulmonary edema and hard-to-control hypertension with right renal artery stenosis on Doppler.
Access: right common femoral artery, ultrasound guided.
Findings: selective right renal angiography confirms significant stenosis of the right renal artery. Left renal artery without significant stenosis.
Intervention: a single balloon-expandable stent placed across the right renal artery lesion with good angiographic result and no residual stenosis. Brisk flow to the right kidney afterward.
Closure device to the access site. No complications.
Plan: aspirin indefinitely; clopidogrel 75 mg daily for 3 months, then stop. Renal artery duplex in about 1 month.

Principal diagnosis: secondary (renovascular) hypertension due to right renal artery stenosis, with recurrent nocturnal dyspnea after flash pulmonary edema in September.

History: since her September admission she has had repeated episodes of waking acutely breathless at night that ease when she sits upright, the last two nights in a row. Takes hydrochlorothiazide and amlodipine with metoprolol succinate for blood pressure.

Exam on admission: BP 162/98. Bruit audible over the right upper quadrant of the abdomen. Lungs and heart otherwise as documented in the H&P.

Data: creatinine 1.5 (elevated), BUN 28 (elevated), potassium 4.2. Urinalysis without protein or blood. Renal artery Doppler: significant right renal artery stenosis.

Course: one dose of IV furosemide on arrival with relief of her breathlessness. Nephrology and interventional radiology consulted. Given recurrent flash pulmonary edema, she underwent right renal angiography with placement of a single stent on 10/13 (see procedure note), uncomplicated. No further night-time episodes during the stay. Blood pressure lower in the days after the stent.

Discharge medications: NEW clopidogrel 75 mg daily for 3 months. Continue metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, amlodipine 10 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily, lithium carbonate 300 mg BID, sertraline 100 mg daily.

Follow-up: PCP within one week with BMP; nephrology with renal artery duplex in one month.

documents.title: ICU and Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: critical care
documents.body:
Outside hospital admission 06/12/2026 to 06/16/2026 (medical ICU 06/12-06/14, then medical floor).

Principal diagnosis: severe lithium toxicity, recurrent.

Presentation: 59-year-old woman with bipolar I disorder on long-term lithium, previous lithium toxicity in April 2025, renovascular hypertension s/p right renal artery stent (10/2025), diet-controlled type 2 diabetes and hyperlipidemia. Two days of severe and worsening nausea, vomiting, diarrhea and hand tremor, with confusion and unsteadiness on her feet, much like last year. Denies any recent illness, travel or change in diet.

Home medications on admission: lithium carbonate 300 mg BID, metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, amlodipine 10 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily, sertraline 100 mg daily.
Allergies: ACE inhibitors, shellfish.

On arrival: BP 130/85, HR 92, RR 18, temperature 37.1 C (98.8 F). Alert but distressed. Mild ataxia and a fine tremor of both hands. Otherwise nonfocal.
Labs: lithium 2.5 mmol/L (therapeutic 0.6-1.2). Sodium 140, potassium 4.2, creatinine 1.1. TSH 2.5.

Course: admitted to the ICU for neuro checks and close monitoring. Lithium held. Aggressive IV isotonic fluids. Nephrology consulted; with preserved urine output and falling levels, dialysis was not needed. Lithium 1.6 the next morning and 0.9 on 06/14, when she moved to the floor. Tremor, confusion and gait normalized by 06/15.

Discharge plan:
- Hydrochlorothiazide STOPPED: thiazides reduce lithium clearance and this is her second toxicity on the combination.
- Lithium on HOLD until reviewed by her psychiatrist this week.
- Continue metoprolol succinate, amlodipine, atorvastatin, aspirin, sertraline.
- PCP within one week to follow blood pressure off the thiazide.
